islands.law:
# The atlas's value wave, as a law of nature. Transcribed from Atlas._wave:
#
#     V = max(source, best neighbour * (1 - decay)^distance) * passable
#
# with decay 0.06 (0.94 per orthogonal step, 0.94^sqrt2 = 0.916214 per diagonal)
# and a solid cell letting `leak` of the wave through — the harness's per-cell
# leak, innate then taught per hue by what pressing on it did.
# max8 also contains the four orthogonal neighbours, but they are discounted
# more there than under max4, so the max of the two is exactly the eight-way
# wave with a diagonal that costs sqrt 2. The harness paints source and solid
# each thought, steps this `subticks` times, and reads value at the centre.

channel source
channel solid
channel value

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(source, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Confinement suppression (night lab 2026-09-23, champion #35): a source hemmed in by
# solid counts less, so local food in a nook stops dominating and the frontier wins there.
# 24.5 meals on 32 never-seen FINAL worlds vs 18.8 the reference wave, 17.1 the tuned ghost.

channel source
channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel here
channel value
channel confinement
channel injection

# Measure local solidity to detect dead-ends/corridors.
# High sum8(solid) means tight space.
rule calc_conf:
  when 1
  set confinement = sum8(solid)

# Inject signals, but suppress heavily if in a tight space.
# The division by (1 + k*conf) reduces value in dead-ends.
# This prevents the agent from being pulled into local maxima in confined areas.
rule inject:
  when 1
  set injection = max(thing, source) / (1 + 0.5 * confinement)

# Propagate the value wave.
# Use standard Bellman decay. The suppressed injection ensures dead-ends don't dominate.
rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(injection, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Sources linger: a commitment law. The smell of a thing behind a wall is
# painted where the world's geodesic bearing points, and that bearing flips
# between the two ways round as the agent takes a step each way (seen on world
# 7: eleven frames out of twelve on the same spot, the source hopping left and
# right of it). Here a painted source keeps ~94% of itself per thought after
# the paint moves on, so the wave still holds the place it was first told and
# the nearer of the two stays the target. Where the agent stands there is
# nothing: `here` and its ring erase the ghost (an eaten morsel leaves no
# ghost to circle).

channel source
channel solid
channel here
channel value
channel ghost: init 0

rule linger:
  when 1
  set ghost = max(source, 0.99 * ghost) * (1 - here) * (1 - max8(here))

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(ghost, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

control.best:
# Confinement suppression (night lab 2026-09-23, champion #35): a source hemmed in by
# solid counts less, so local food in a nook stops dominating and the frontier wins there.
# 24.5 meals on 32 never-seen FINAL worlds vs 18.8 the reference wave, 17.1 the tuned ghost.

channel source
channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel here
channel value
channel confinement
channel injection

# Measure local solidity to detect dead-ends/corridors.
# High sum8(solid) means tight space.
rule calc_conf:
  when 0.9331
  set confinement = sum8(solid)

# Inject signals, but suppress heavily if in a tight space.
# The division by (1 + k*conf) reduces value in dead-ends.
# This prevents the agent from being pulled into local maxima in confined areas.
rule inject:
  when 0.7889
  set injection = max(thing, source) / (0.8719 + 0.4593 * confinement)

# Propagate the value wave.
# Use standard Bellman decay. The suppressed injection ensures dead-ends don't dominate.
rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(injection, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.6834 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

theory:
HELPS: how the wave SPREADS matters most. Confinement (sources hemmed in by solid count less, #1) lifted Bellman 14.8 -> 25.7. Per-cell step cost (cheap known-free, dear unknown, #6) is the real champion: holdout 33.6 against the tuned control's 27.0. Weighting frontier marks by the size of what lies beyond (#4) helped train, less holdout.
HURTS: every footprint memory (trail #3, wear #5, boredom #8) loses 1-6 meals. Penalising where I stood bends the wave away from good corridors and food that respawns. Frustration on pressed stone (#7) gained nothing and dropped on holdout. Lingering sources alone are weak (#2).
FAILURE: sealed pockets (world 16). Once a pocket is mapped it holds no frontier, and confinement mutes everything near its walls, so the wave goes flat and the agent paces. It presses one stone and never tries the brown, leaky cells.
UNTRIED: when the reachable region holds no source, an escape wave seeded at the most leaky solids; commitment/heading; using `bad`; a distance discount from the agent.

observations.text: The agent is born in a small sealed pocket under the rock massif, a strip roughly 4x12 cells walled on every side, and spends all 3511 ticks pacing back and forth inside it until it starves, without ever reaching food. Food is close: berries lie just outside the pocket to the lower left and in the room to the right, and the brown cells in the pocket's walls look like doors or rubble that would have let it out. It does try to get out (205 idle presses), but it never opens a door or chips anything, so it keeps pressing the same stone that will not give. Two parts of the law work against it here: once the pocket is mapped there are no frontier sources inside, and the confinement divisor `1/(1 + 0.5*sum8(solid))` damps exactly the cells along the walls where any way out must begin. The fix I would name is a bounded "tried" memory channel: it builds up on solid cells next to `here` while the agent stands pressing them, decays slowly, and multiplies that cell's leak by (1 - tried). Then the wave stops flowing through stone it has already pushed on and moves round the wall to the next untried segment, which is where the doors are.

turns.hypothesis: The map gets a FOOTPRINT memory: a slowly fading `trail` of where the agent has stood, scrolling with the map. Remembered sources (a `ghost` that lingers at 0.99) are wiped wherever the agent has walked, and smelled sources painted onto trodden ground lose most of their weight, while seen morsels keep full weight. Poisoned cells (`bad`) block the wave. This breaks the smell trap, where the bearing flips and leads the agent back and forth over the same cells. Ground the agent has already searched stops calling, so the wave goes to sources it has not checked yet and to the frontier, and the confinement damping keeps nooks from dominating.

Every frontier mark is painted at the same 0.12, so a crack in a wall that leads nowhere pulls the agent as hard as the mouth of a big unexplored region. I add an `openness` field (unknown territory, smoothed a few rings out) and weight frontier sources by it, so exploration flows toward where the most unseen ground is, while food sources keep confinement suppression and burned cells stop the wave. On worlds where meals come from exploring, the agent should reach new food faster and waste fewer trips into small pockets.

The map gets a WEAR memory: footprints accumulate (bounded) where the agent stands and spread into a halo of worn ground, so a smell that keeps pointing into ground the agent has already circled loses its pull (the geodesic-bearing limit cycle breaks) while seen morsels keep full weight. Frontier near worn ground is mildly discounted and the wave passes trodden cells slightly less well, so the agent prefers fresh routes and unexplored territory once it starts looping — this should rescue the trap worlds (world 16) without hurting the direct approach to visible food.

The wave stops spreading at one flat price: each cell now has its own step cost. Known-free ground is cheap (0.95), unknown ground is expensive (0.89, because it may hide a wall), and ground hugging walls costs more. Diagonal spreading is also blocked where it would cut a solid corner. Plans then follow corridors the agent has actually seen and go through door centres, instead of straight lines through imagined space into walls. This should cut the time lost bumping and re-planning when a guessed shortcut turns out to be stone. The agent turns to the unknown only when the frontier is worth it.

The map gets a per-cell FRUSTRATION memory (`tried`): a solid cell the wave keeps leading the agent into accumulates "I pressed here and it did not give", which closes that cell's leak locally (independent of the per-hue lesson, which is too coarse or too slow when one stone sits on the smell's bearing) and kills the pull through it. In the same move, wall faces that separate known-free ground from unknown ground become faint CRACK sources weighted by leak and by (1 - tried), not divided by confinement — so a sealed pocket (world 16) gets systematically probed wall cell by wall cell, doors and rubble first because their taught leak is high, instead of one stone being pressed 205 times; in op

The map learns BOREDOM: a bounded footprint `trail` piles up where the agent keeps standing, and where it exceeds what one passing visit leaves, the ground is `worn` (spread as a decaying flood through free cells). Walls bordering worn ground, and not yet pressed in vain (`tried`), turn into dig sources weighted by their taught leak and the unknown behind them, and boredom raises how much wave those untried walls let through — so a sealed or looping agent stops pacing and probes its walls one after another, each refused stone closing as the next lights up, until a door or rubble gives (world 16), while an agent that keeps walking never wears anything and runs the #6 wave unchanged.
